beats.say: Forty-four caps. For one of the world's best keepers.

card.kicker: ONE OF THE WORLD'S BEST KEEPERS

beats.say: Case file one: Marc-André ter Stegen. Seven Spanish titles and a Champions League with Barcelona.

card.sub: top of European football for almost his whole career

beats.say: The problem? Manuel Neuer. Jürgen Klopp: for a long time, he was behind Manuel Neuer while still being one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

card.sub: “For a long time, he was behind Manuel Neuer…” — Jürgen Klopp

beats.say: In many other eras, he could easily have over one hundred caps. And that's not even the twist.

card.label: what he *could* have had
card.sub: “…he could easily have over 100 caps to his name”

beats.say: After the twenty twenty-six World Cup exit, Neuer retired from international football. For the second time.

card.sub: retired from international football for the second time

beats.say: Then Klopp named his starter. For now, Marc-André ter Stegen will be the goalkeeper who starts the first game.

card.text:
FOR NOW, MARC-ANDRÉ
TER STEGEN WILL BE
THE GOALKEEPER WHO
*STARTS* THE FIRST GAME.

beats.say: He's thirty-four, on loan at Ajax, and now Germany's most experienced goalkeeper.

card.kicker: NOW · AJAX, ON LOAN FROM BARÇA
card.label: Germany's most *experienced* keeper
card.sub: 44 caps · the frontrunner for the national team

beats.say: So, was he the unluckiest keeper of his generation? Follow for the next Scout File.
